name: Map colouring: G = W wipes out E (look-ahead vs forward checking)
note: Constructed to match the lecture's observation (the course notes are not reproduced here). Regions G, N, S, E; colours W (white), R (red), Y (yellow). G touches N and S; E touches N and S; G and E do not touch. D(G) = {W,R,Y}, D(N) = {W,R}, D(S) = {W,Y}, D(E) = {R,Y}. After G = W, forward checking leaves N = {R}, S = {Y} and does NOT touch E (E is not a neighbour of G), so D(E) = {R,Y} still looks fine. Full look-ahead or arc consistency revises E against N and S: R and Y both lose their support, D(E) is empty, so G = W is rejected at once. Forward checking only finds out two assignments later.
